Definition: from a compound of G2556 and G3056; to revile:--curse, speak evil of.
BiblicalUsage: Kakologeo is to speak evil of — to revile, to curse. The law says he that curseth father or mother, let him die the death, and Jesus throws it back at the Pharisees who set aside the commandment; and the silversmiths at Ephesus spoke evil of the Way before the multitude.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe cursing a parent or reviling the gospel are the same sin wearing different clothes: contempt spoken aloud. The tongue that curses is the heart showing itself, and that is why I watch mine.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
